hao-outer-dmet-loop-global-potential: Methods, p.12: after Step 5 the paper defines its two nested loops; inner VQE loop updates theta and x, outer DMET loop optimizes mu. The second quote is a claim, but the value does not assert it.
hao-alternating-optimization: Methods, p.10: Eqs. 19-21 define the constrained problem and the alternating x-then-theta update, repeated until convergence.
hao-uccsd-ansatz: Preliminaries, p.7: 'Here, we use the Unitary Coupled-Cluster Singles and Doubles (UCCSD) ansatz' and VQE for the embedding Hamiltonian; Eqs. 12-14.
hao-parameter-shift-gradient: Methods, p.11: the paper states it computes the circuit-parameter derivative with parameter-shift rules (refs 41, 42), after Eq. 22.
hao-h4-setup: Results and discussion, p.13: STO-3G, 8 qubits for the full system, each atom one fragment (4 fragments), at most 4 qubits per fragment. All stated as the paper's own setup.
hao-h4-dmet-little-advantage: Results and discussion, p.13: the authors say DMET on so small a system may not give substantial resource savings and H4 only demonstrates the method. A limit on their own result.
hao-h2o2-parameters: Results and discussion, pp.14-15: four geometric parameters d2, d1, theta, phi, with the angles defined at p.15 (O atom as origin). Own setup. No figure-read value is in this item.
hao-glycolic-ohrotation-setup: Results and discussion, p.15: the OH group is rotated as a fixed-point rigid body about its bonded C atom, by Ry then Rz; the parameters optimized were Rz and Ry. The paper's own scope.
hao-future-work-scope: Conclusions, p.17: 'Future research will focus on expanding its scope to periodic materials, incorporating advanced quantum hardware capabilities'. The authors name this as work not yet done.
dmet-vqe-future-noise: Conclusions, p.17 (the stored quote says p.16; the sentence is on p.17): future work on error mitigation and noise-resilient algorithms. The authors name it as not yet done. The stored quote location should read p.17.
harvey-models-defined-pqc-tensor-network: Abstract, p.1: the authors introduce complex-valued tensor network models for sequence processing, built from parameterised quantum circuits, with inductive bias from the architecture; defined in Section 2.
harvey-binary-classification-scope: Section 3, p.7: 'We focus on tasks of binary classification, ie only a single qubit (q'=1) is measured'. Scope of the experiments.
harvey-postselection-overhead: Section 2, p.4: the authors caveat that postselection is not free on a quantum device and costs an exponential sampling overhead in the postselected qubits. A caveat on their own models' hardware use; the standard fact is background. True type: stated limit, not theoretical.
harvey-models-species-hyperparameters: Section 2, p.4: 'The number of qubits per wire q, the specific form, or ansatz, of each PQC ... and the choice for the perp-effect are hyperparameters of our models'.
harvey-tree-scheme-size: Section 2.2, p.4: defines the tree scheme; |S|-1 m-boxes (sum formula given) and depth log|S|.
harvey-conv-fbox-count: Section 2.4, p.6: defines conv; m-boxes |S|-1, depth log|S|, f-boxes |S|-(log|S|+1) with the sum formula. Quotes are verbatim; the text layer only garbles the minus signs.
harvey-sliding-window-ctns: Section 2.4, p.6: 'a sliding variant ... CTNS' with a fixed window w scanning the sequence, outputs aggregated by the average.
harvey-software-and-ansatz: Section 3, p.8: DisCoPy, Bobcat, tensornetwork, JAX; results use ansatz 14 of ref [80] because it had the best test performance (the paper says test performance, a selection detail).
harvey-training-protocol-single-seed: Section 3, p.8: AdamW, binary cross-entropy, validation early stopping, fixed seed for all models, test accuracy at best validation accuracy, 'rather than an averaged behaviour'. Own protocol.
harvey-datasets-three: Section 3, p.8: the three datasets (clickbait, Rotten Tomatoes, DNA binding affinity) named as the paper's own data.
harvey-dataset-sizes: Table captions, p.9: Table 2 25,312/3,165/3,165; Table 3 8,362/1,046/1,046; Table 4 (reduced Clickbait) 2,033/763/763; Tables 5-6 1,600/200/200. Checked against the page text.
harvey-scalable-model-scope-and-reduced-: Section 3, p.8 states PTN/TTN/STN are scalable, CTN/SCTN harder to scale, Tables 2-3 show only scalable models, and a reduced Clickbait dataset is used for SCTN. A limit on its own simulations.
harvey-sctn-100-structures: Appendix B.3, p.21: SCTN contraction cannot be factorised, so only the 100 most frequent syntactic structures are used. A restriction on their own SCTN results.
harvey-hardware-setup-h2-1: Section 3.1, p.9 and Figure 6 caption, p.10: uSTN, rSTN, uCTN with discard on H2-1 (32 qubits, quantum volume 2^16 as reported), 300 shots. The examples are a 'representative selection', which the value says as 'selection'.
harvey-born-rule-only-nonlinearity: Section 4, p.12: 'in our efficiently simulable models, we have only used the Born rule as a nonlinearity'. States what the paper's models use.
harvey-uniform-parameter-count-formula: Table 7, p.20, checked on the rendered page: uPTN, uTTN and uSTN each have D(|theta_w||V| + |theta_m| + |theta_c|). The paper's own parameter count.
harville-review-scope-three-themes: Abstract, pp.1-2: the paper states the three themes it emphasizes.
harville-benchmark-scope-illustrative: Section 5, p.32: 'original, illustrative benchmarks ... intended to illustrate, rather than definitively rank'; ADAPT-VQE and USCC against UCCSD-VQE and coupled cluster, FCI as reference.
harville-benchmark-noiseless-no-gate-cou: Section 5, p.32: the benchmarks are noiseless simulation and miss the noise tradeoff; two-qubit gate counts are discussed qualitatively. The paper's own limits on its own benchmarks.
harville-benchmark-basis-sets-systems: Section 5.1, p.33: STO-3G, errors against FCI for non-symmetric H2O, BeH2 and H6 (Figure 4). The paper's own setup. The H4 6-31G comparison is a different section.
hasanzadeh-uc-four-method-groups: Section I, p.1: 'organizes existing research into four methodological groups' (annealing, variational/hybrid, QML-assisted, quantum-inspired metaheuristics).
hasanzadeh-uc-survey-scope: Abstract, p.1: the paper is a survey of quantum computing for the unit commitment problem, categorized by the four paradigms. 'Comprehensive' is self-description, but the value states it as scope only.
dvqe-v3-what-is-proposed: Abstract, p.1 (arXiv v3): proposes a two-stage DVQE software for QUBO and bounded QP, with monolithic and distributed execution and bitstring-based QUBO evaluation.
dvqe-v3-two-stage-training: Section 3.1, pp.6-7: defines the two stages, gradient-free warm start with BH, GWO or ABC, then sampling-based refinement.
dvqe-v3-warmstart-over-parameters-not-bi: Section 3.1, pp.7-8: the warm start searches the continuous parameter vector theta, not the binary vector z, with every candidate evaluated by circuit execution and measurement. The paper's own definition of its stage.
dvqe-v3-spsa-two-evals: Section 3.1, p.8: the refinement update uses theta+ and theta-, two sampled energies per iteration, shown in the update equations.
dvqe-v3-cost-based-decoding: Section 3.1, p.8: z* = argmin C(z) over the final histogram support; the stated reason (most frequent is not necessarily lowest cost) is a plain consequence of the rule.
dvqe-v3-diskit-distributed-remap: Section 3.2, p.8: 'The implementation uses Qiskit for circuit construction and simulation, and Diskit for distributed circuit remapping.'
dvqe-v3-qqp-no-slack-one-bit: Abstract, p.1 and Section 3.3: defines QQP as a sequence of local one-bit QUBOs, each bit a local up or down move in a trust region, with no slack variables.
dvqe-v3-qqp-dimension-n: Section 3.3, p.14: Eqs. 43-48 construct the local QUBO with one bit per continuous variable, so its dimension is n. A direct consequence of the paper's own construction, shown on the page.
dvqe-v3-qqp-accept-reject: Section 3.3, p.15: Eqs. 51-53 define acceptance if the alpha objective improves by more than tau_f, otherwise rejection and a smaller step. The reason given is a plain consequence of the rule.
dvqe-v3-lp-special-case: Section 3.3, p.15: 'bounded LP problems can also be handled as the special case obtained by setting the quadratic objective matrix to zero'; Section 4.0.3 uses A=0 for LP instances.
dvqe-v3-ablation-setup: Section 4.0.1, p.19: n=6..15, 8 seeds each, 80 instances, 5 variants, 400 runs, brute-force exact optimum.
dvqe-v3-ablation-limit-not-max-accuracy: Section 4.0.1, p.19: the authors state the ablation is not a maximum-accuracy tuning study and higher success rates 'could likely' be obtained with more resources. A caveat on their own experiment.
dvqe-v3-ablation-training-settings: Section 4.0.1, p.20: depth 1, learning rate 0.05, at most 80 iterations, 256 and 2000 shots, population 6, 8 warm-start iterations, 64 shots, CVaR alpha 0.2, QPU layout [4,4,4,4,4,4].
dvqe-v3-gurobi-purpose-setup: Section 4.0.2, p.20: not a speed claim, Gurobi MIQP as exact reference, n=3..18 with 5 seeds each (80 instances). The paper's own setup.
dvqe-v3-gurobi-settings: Section 4.0.2, pp.20-21: depth 1, learning rate 0.5, at most 80 iterations, 512 and 5000 shots, BH population 12, 20 warm-start iterations, 512 shots, CVaR alpha 0.1, layout [4,4,4,4,4].
dvqe-v3-qqp-validation-setup: Section 4.0.3, pp.21-22: QP and LP instances n=3..32, one easy and one hard per dimension, success if max of the three percentage gaps is at most 1%.
dvqe-v3-qqp-timing-overhead: Section 4.0.3, p.22: 'the timing results should be interpreted as software overhead, not as a claim of runtime advantage', because DVQE runs on CPU circuit software and QQP may need many local QUBO calls. A limit on their own timing results.
dvqe-v3-large-scale-classical-backend: Section 4.0.4, p.23: this experiment uses a classical random-restart bit-flip local-search QUBO backend inside QQP, not DVQE, because the aim is algorithmic scalability. The paper states this itself.
dvqe-v3-large-scale-reference-solver: Section 4.0.4, p.23: for n=150 and n=300 the reference solver reports a positive directional derivative message, so these references are numerical comparison points, not certified optima. A limit the paper states on its own comparison.
dvqe-no-speedup-simulator: Section 5, p.24: 'This work does not claim quantum speedup, since the experiments are performed using a CPU-based quantum-circuit software'; Section 1 p.3 names Qiskit Aer as the simulation backend. The stored anchors say p.23; the text is on pp.24 and 3.
